items.note: The page states the chirp formula $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot\frac{a*(\overline a\cdot u)}{T}$ with the correct $a$ and links bluestein-chirp.md, as instructed; it is not derived here. The hypothesis that every $t_i$ is even appears in the setup.

It defines $(R_cz)_j=z_{cj}$ for a unit $c$, substitutes $h=ck$ (noting this permutes residues), and gets $(F_q^+R_cz)_j=\frac1q\sum_hz_he^{2\pi ihc^{-1}j/q}=(R_c^{-1}F_q^+z)_j$, which is correct. It then identifies $R=\bigotimes_iR_{t_i}$, uses that each $t_i$ is a unit mod $s_i$, and tensors to $F^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=R^{-1}F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$ and then $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$, exactly as in paper ll. 3953-3962.

It uses the commutation of a coordinate permutation with coordinatewise products to get $R(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\cdot F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$, applies $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$, and then uses $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ and $F^+_{\boldsymbol s}F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$ to reach $\frac1SF^+_{\boldsymbol s}F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=\frac{u*v}{S^2}$. Both normalizations agree with the paper's $1/q$-normalized $F_q,F_q^+$ (ll. 3506-3511, 3973-3982).
